stem:
Chitra builds matchstick squares in a row. Position 1 uses 4 sticks, position 2 uses 7 sticks, and position 3 uses 10 sticks. She wants the position number n whose arrangement uses 40 sticks.

Which approach is correct?

options.text: Describe only the matchstick arrangement in words, without a rule in n.
Use the rule 3n + 1 for any pretty drawing, even one not in this sequence.
Use the rule 3n + 1 for this sequence and solve 3n + 1 = 40 to find n.
Pick n = 40, because 40 is the target number printed in the question.

teacher.key_rationale: The sequence grows by 3 sticks each time from a start of 4, so position n uses 3n + 1 sticks. Set 3n + 1 = 40 and solve. A word sketch without the rule in n misses the hinge. Applying the rule off-sequence drops the belonging condition. Reading n off the target 40 is surface capture.
